title: Gear-Driven Assembly Line Simulator
description: The user operates an industrial assembly line where interlocking gears power a conveyor system that processes animated boxes. Players must calibrate gear speed, torque direction, conveyor belt tension, sorting gates, and quality thresholds to successfully route boxes through inspection stations without jamming the machinery.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load 'shared_assets/gears.glb' and 'shared_assets/BoxAnimated.glb'. Scene setup: place the gears model on the left side as the power source of an assembly line. Create a visual conveyor belt using a series of thin box geometries with animated UV-scrolling material stretching from the gears to the right. Clone the BoxAnimated model 5 times and place them queued at the start of the conveyor. Play each box's built-in animation using AnimationMixer. Camera: perspective at position (0, 8, 15) looking at origin. Lighting: ambient light (0.4 intensity) plus two directional lights from upper-left and upper-right. Add a ground plane with grid texture. Build an HTML control panel overlay with these interactive steps requiring parameter validation: (1) A 'Gear Speed' slider (range 0.1-3.0, default 1.0) that controls gear model rotation speed on Y-axis. (2) A 'Torque Direction' toggle (CW/CCW) that reverses gear rotation and conveyor scroll direction. (3) A 'Belt Tension' slider (0.1-2.0) controlling how fast boxes translate along the conveyor — validate that tension cannot exceed 1.5x gear speed or show a warning. (4) A 'Sorting Gate' dropdown with 3 lanes (Accept/Rework/Reject) that determines where the current front box routes to — animate box moving to corresponding offset lane. (5) A 'Quality Threshold' number input (1-100) that auto-assigns gate lane based on a random quality score displayed per box. (6) A 'Start Line' button that begins the simulation loop, processing boxes one by one with 2-second intervals. (7) A 'Pause/Resume' button. (8) A 'Reset' button restoring all defaults and box positions. Display a live dashboard showing boxes processed, current gear RPM, and jam warnings when parameters conflict. Gears should visually spin proportional to speed setting. All parameter changes must validate ranges and show inline error messages for invalid inputs.
